## Review — ACCEPT, and the open question is answered: **A, as shipped**

Reviewer of record: `domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`. Clean against `origin/main` `f626808d4` (`merge-tree` exit 0), changeset present, 4 files.

### ⭐ The catch that matters: the naive fix would have re-introduced the bug

> the label must snap the owning **COLUMN's** start date, not the interpolated instant under the pixel, because a week column can straddle a month boundary and `headerGroups` keys such a column by the month its start falls in

That is the review's whole value. Interpolating the date under the left-edge pixel is the obvious implementation, it passes any test written at a non-boundary scroll position, and it would have made the toolbar and the band header **disagree for part of every straddling week** — the exact defect this card exists to fix, surviving in a narrower window where it is far harder to spot than "January 2026 over August columns".

The second refinement is the same shape: `visibleRange` compares `offsets[i+1] < from` strictly, so at an exact period boundary it names the *previous* cell. Correct as virtualization overscan, wrong for "which period owns the left edge" — so it was not reused. Two available helpers, both nearly right, both rejected for stated reasons.

### The measurement could not have been done in the DOM harness, and the report says why

> happy-dom reports `clientWidth` 0 and therefore **never fires the auto-scroll-to-Today effect** — which is the card's whole first-paint repro

So the jsdom-family harness cannot reproduce this defect at all. Not "is unreliable here" — *cannot*. A lane that had asserted green from the DOM tests alone would have been measuring a page that never scrolled.

Real Chromium at `/opt/pw-browsers`, 1440×900, four scroll positions, with the **before** leg run on the same page by reverting the label expression in place under the same trap-and-hash discipline:

| | toolbar | band | agree |
|---|---|---|---|
| **after**, 4 positions | Aug 2026 / Sep 2026 / Aug 2026 / Dec 2025 | matches at each | ✅ ×4 |
| **before**, same 4 | `December 2025` at **all four** | — | ❌ ❌ ❌ ✅ |

The single accidental agreement in the before leg is the point: at scrollLeft 0 a static range-start label is correct, which is precisely why a one-position test would have passed against the broken code.

### Public surface verified independently

The report says the four new period helpers were un-exported so the package surface is unchanged. Checked rather than accepted: **18 exported symbols in `GanttView.tsx` on `main`, 18 on this branch.** Worth doing deliberately — adding helpers to a published module's surface is how a repair quietly becomes a compatibility commitment, and this one avoided it.

### Ablations

Both predicted before running, both exact. Leg A (label reverted to `timelineRange.start`) → 5 failed / 2 passed, *"and the five are the predicted five"*; the two that stay green are the single-month control and the left-edge clamp — **the only two a static January label satisfies**. Leg B (both `onClick`s removed) → 2 failed / 5 passed.

⭐ And the no-rebuild leg is declared as load-bearing rather than skipped: the test imports `./GanttView` relatively and the root vitest config aliases the package to `src`, so no `dist/` sits on the resolution path. That is the difference between "I didn't rebuild" and "a rebuild cannot affect this result".

`check:readme-exports` correctly recorded **NOT MEASURED** on its own population-collapse banner (24 of 40 packages unbuilt, *"this run proves nothing"*), *and* shown inert to this diff by measurement — README fenced blocks 38 before / 38 after, `src/index.tsx` byte-identical. `check:i18n-dead-keys` recorded as a report, no colour, because it says so itself.

### Answering the open question: **A**, and it is already right

You read "one unit of the current granularity" as the **label's tier** (month under day/week, year under month/quarter, decade under year, shift-day under segmented day) rather than one column of the active viewMode. **Confirmed.**

Your own argument settles it: under B, one click in month view moves one month, so the label is unchanged for **11 of 12 clicks** — and the steppers were wired *because* the label change gave them something real to drive. B satisfies the sentence and defeats the purpose the ruling gave it. A also required no per-viewMode invention, which was the thing I asked you to report rather than paper over.

No change needed. It is pinned and documented.

### Filed alongside

**#7228** — `columnWidthForContainer` branches on container width and returns 110 from **all three** arms, so the breakpoint table it documents cannot change the result, while the two sibling sizing helpers beside it use the same breakpoints and do vary. Grading it now. Good instinct to file rather than fix: it is in the same file as #7204 / #7224, which are blocked on an open maintainer decision about exactly these width gates.
